title: Financial Advisory Office Scope Tasks: High-Touch and Floor Maintenance Routines for Wealth Management Firms
seoTitle: Financial Advisory Office Scope Tasks: Daily, Weekly & Monthly Checklist
metaDescription: Financial advisory office scope tasks by frequency, with labor minutes and the specialty items that push hours past 3,500 sq ft/hr. Compare quotes.
excerpt: A wealth management office needs a scope of work that separates client-facing detail work from routine back-office cleaning. This checklist assigns every task a frequency and labor estimate, and flags the specialty items that justify higher hourly rates.
quickAnswer: A financial advisory office scope should split tasks into every-visit client-path care (reception, conference rooms, restrooms, kitchenette), weekly detail work (millwork dusting, glass partitions, private offices), and monthly or quarterly floor care. Routine areas clean at about 3,500 sq ft per hour, but glass conference rooms, hardwood reception floors, and clean-desk confidential handling can drop productivity to 2,200-2,800 sq ft per hour. Those specialty tasks are why advisory bids often run 15-25 percent above a generic office of the same size.

blocks.text: Start With Zones, Not a Generic Checklist

Most janitorial scopes are written as a single list of tasks applied to the whole suite. That format works for a call center, but it fails in a wealth management office, where a 400 sq ft reception area and a 250 sq ft client conference room carry more reputational weight than the other 5,000 sq ft combined. Before assigning frequencies, divide the floor plan into four zones: the client path, restrooms and kitchenette, private advisor and operations offices, and restricted rooms such as file storage and the server closet.

Each zone gets its own frequency and its own quality standard. The client path is cleaned to presentation standard every visit. Restrooms and the kitchenette are sanitized every visit. Private offices are serviced on rotation, with trash and recycling every visit but vacuuming and dusting once or twice weekly. Restricted rooms are entered only when the firm schedules access, usually monthly, and often with an employee present.
Every-Visit Tasks for the Client Path and Restrooms

blocks.caption: Every-visit scope for a 6,000 sq ft advisory suite cleaned three nights weekly
rows: Dust-mop and damp-mop hardwood, spot-clean entry glass, wipe reception counter
No visible grit or smudges at 3 ft
Wipe glass table, chair arms, AV remotes and conference phone; vacuum; streak-check partition glass at handle height
Zero fingerprints at table and door
Disinfect fixtures and touch points, polish mirror and chrome, restock, mop with neutral cleaner
Disinfect fixtures, restock, spot-mop, empty sanitary bins
Wipe counters, sink, microwave inside and out, fridge handles, coffee machine exterior
Empty trash and recycling (not shred consoles), replace liners
Disinfect door handles, light switches, elevator call buttons in suite lobby
EPA-registered disinfectant, label dwell time met

blocks.text: Those seven lines alone total about 81 minutes, or 1.35 labor hours, before any vacuuming of private offices. At a standard rate of $35-$65 per hour, that is $47-$88 of labor per visit spent on roughly 1,800 sq ft of high-visibility space. That ratio is the core reason advisory bids do not match the simple 3,500 sq ft per hour productivity assumption.

items: Vacuum private advisor offices and operations workstations on a rotation so each office is fully vacuumed at least twice weekly on a three-night schedule.
Damp-wipe credenzas, bookshelves, and wood millwork with a microfiber cloth; avoid moving papers, portfolios, or anything on desks under the firm's clean-desk policy.
Clean both faces of interior glass partitions and sidelights top to bottom, not just at handle height.
Edge-vacuum carpet along baseboards and under the reception desk kick plate.
Wipe chair bases, conference chair casters, and the underside of conference table edges where hand oil accumulates.
Descale restroom faucets and polish stainless partitions.
Dust HVAC diffusers and return grilles reachable from a step stool.

blocks.text: Floor care is where scope disputes start, because many base contracts quietly exclude it. Engineered hardwood in reception needs a weekly or every-visit dust-mop pass followed by a low-moisture microfiber wet pass, then a periodic deep clean and screen-and-recoat every 12-24 months depending on traffic. Carpet tiles in private offices and corridors need spot extraction monthly and hot-water extraction quarterly or semiannually. Any VCT in the kitchenette or file room needs scrubbing and recoating once or twice a year.

Budget those deep programs separately. Our benchmark amortizes quarterly floor care at $0.03-$0.06 per sq ft per month, which for a 6,000 sq ft suite equals $180-$360 per month. Requiring that number as a distinct line item stops vendors from cutting nightly labor to pay for an extraction visit.

blocks.title: Tools that keep hardwood and stone looking new
blocks.text: A Rubbermaid Commercial 36-Inch Cotton Dust Mop with a 60-inch handle and 360-degree swivel clears grit from wide reception and corridor floors in a few passes before any wet work. For the wet pass on wood, the Bona Commercial System Multi-Surface Hardwood Mop Kit pairs an 18-inch aluminum base and telescoping handle with washable microfiber dusting and wet pads designed to be wood safe. Where VCT or tile needs mopping, an Unger 15-Gallon Dual-Bucket SmartColor System keeps clean solution in one red or blue compartment and dirty rinse water in the other, preventing re-soiling.
Specialty Tasks That Push Labor Above Standard Office Rates

When you compare an advisory proposal to a generic office benchmark, expect a premium tied to specific tasks. The table below shows how each one affects productivity and where a vendor is likely to bill specialty hourly rates of $55-$95 rather than standard rates of $35-$65.

blocks.text: Writing the Scope Into Your Contract

items.name: Attach a zone map
items.text: Mark client path, restrooms, offices, and restricted rooms on the floor plan and attach it as an exhibit so every bidder prices the same thing.

items.name: Assign a frequency to every task
items.text: Use every visit, weekly, monthly, and quarterly columns. Avoid vague terms such as as needed for anything recurring.

items.name: Define what the crew must not touch
items.text: Shred consoles, locked cabinets, desk surfaces with papers, and safe rooms should be listed as excluded so the vendor is protected and the firm's confidentiality controls stay intact.

items.name: Separate project work
items.text: Floor refinishing, carpet extraction, and window washing above 10 ft belong in a priced periodic schedule, not the base monthly fee.

items.name: Set inspection checkpoints
items.text: Agree on a monthly walk-through scored against the zone standards, with a defined remedy period for missed items.

blocks.text: Once your zone map and task frequencies are set, run the square footage and add-ons through the Office Cleaning Cost Calculator, then drop each vendor's line items into the Quote Comparator to spot who is under-scoping the client path.

faqs.q: How many labor hours does a 6,000 sq ft financial advisory office need per visit?
faqs.a: At the ISSA reference pace of 3,500 sq ft per hour, the suite would need about 1.7 hours. With the client-path detail, glass, and clean-desk constraints typical of advisory firms, plan on 2.2-2.6 hours per visit. At $35-$65 per hour, that is roughly $77-$169 in direct labor before overhead, supplies, and margin.

faqs.q: Should the cleaning crew empty shred consoles?
faqs.a: No. Locked shred consoles should be serviced only by the shredding contractor under its own chain-of-custody process. Your scope should explicitly exclude them, and crews should be trained to leave any paper next to a console in place and report it.

faqs.q: Do we need an EPA-registered disinfectant for an advisory office?
faqs.a: For restroom fixtures and high-touch points, yes. Use an EPA-registered product and follow the label dwell time. Your vendor must keep Safety Data Sheets available and train staff under OSHA's Hazard Communication standard, 29 CFR 1910.1200.

faqs.q: How often should hardwood reception floors be refinished?
faqs.a: With daily dust-mopping and correct low-moisture wet cleaning, most engineered hardwood in a reception area needs a screen-and-recoat every 12-24 months. Price it as a separate after-hours project rather than folding it into the monthly fee.

faqs.q: Are green-certified products practical in a wealth management office?
faqs.a: Yes. Green Seal or EPA Safer Choice general-purpose cleaners and glass cleaners perform well on the soil levels found in advisory suites. Reserve EPA-registered disinfectants for restrooms, kitchenette touch points, and shared phones and remotes.
